Mr. Prlic as president would create the agenda and invite the members of the HVO HZ HB to the meetings, and at those meetings they would pass this various enactments, appointments and other legislation. As well, it's also from this time onwards that the legislation which was passed at these meetings appears in the Narodni List. One other thing, an addition to the numbered meetings the HVO HZ HB also held what they called either "extraordinary" or "working meetings," which were called to deal with pressing business, and they had quite a number of those as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Before we come to some of the records of these meetings that you've just described, can I next ask you to be shown Exhibits -- well, first of all P 00390. And while the registry is doing that, we will indeed tender P 00429, the appointment of Mr. Prlic. Sir, if you have that document in front of you now, can you tell us what that is and how that relates to or informs -- can you inform the Judges as to what was happening at this particular point, the same day, in fact, that Mr. Prlic was appointed president?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH
utterances.text: Yes. This document, and I apologise for any problems with the translations or the physical layout of the numbering of these. This is the beginning of a report on the meeting of the Presidency of the HZ HB on the 14th of August, 1992. I think it's split up into two exhibits, but it begins with a report on the political situation in the HZ HB given by Mr. Bozo Rajic, and then it moves into minutes of the meeting of the Presidency of the HZ HB. And this is the meeting indeed where a number of new laws were passed or new legislation was passed and in which Mr. Prlic was appointed as president of the HVO HZ HB.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Keeping that document in mind, in fact, if we can go on to P 00391. I believe the reasons will be clear in a moment. Can you tell us, sir, what is Exhibit P 00391?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH
utterances.text: I believe this is -- well, this is the second half of that same basic document that I was discussing earlier. These are actually the minutes of the meeting. The first half of this document is the declaration or the comments on the political situation made by Mr. Rajic, and this is the actual -- I think this is the minutes of the meeting itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If you look, please -- if I can ask that you be shown page 3 of the document. Can you see that in fact the document, the report that we were looking at a moment ago has essentially been incorporated in the minutes of the meeting?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. So we could perhaps work with 391 as the more complete document. Can you tell us, sir -- if I can ask you to be shown, for instance, page 7 of the document. Are these minutes in the sense that also that various statements or comments are attributed to various participants at the meeting?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And in fact, on -- under item number 2, there's a reference to certain comments or information given by, according to this document, by Mr. Stojic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And could I direct your attention to page 11. Under XV, dismissals and appointments do you see that on the same day that Mr. Boban signed his decision on the 14th of August, 1992, does this document indeed reflect the proposal that Mr. Prlic be appointed president of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely, and he's nominated by Mr. Jozo Maric.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Moving forward, sir -- well, we would tender Exhibits P 00390 and P 00391.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just one question so that I can understand this. You said, sir, that when a decree was taken, they would discuss it first during their meetings, and I can see that on page 10, for example, for the establishment of the central bank there was a report made by Mr. Prlic, tabled by Mr. Prlic, and then the decree was passed. Does that mean that all the acts, administrative acts, laws, decrees taken during that period were automatically submitted to this type of meeting? That is to say that this type of meeting was held first before they were adopted and passed. Is that how things worked?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. And I should make it clear exactly which sorts of meetings we're talking about. The meeting here of the 14th of August is a meeting of the Presidency of the HZ HB. What I was discussing earlier were meetings of the Presidency of the HVO HZ HB with the -- in both situations, as far as available evidence shows us, acts were proposed to the general body and discussed or at least formally presented before they were passed. Now, with the HVO HZ HB, any member could propose a draft of legislation to be adopted. It would then be looked at as a matter of course by the commission for regulations, which would look into the legal drafting and to make sure that the law was drafted properly and matched and fit in with the rest of their body of legislation. It would also be looked at by the head of the department of finance for review, and they would be submitted to the meeting as outlined in the decree on executive authority which we just discussed a minute ago. These would then be put on the agenda by the president of the HVO HZ HB, these matters - that was Mr. Prlic - and then at the meeting they would be discussed and voted on. If they had passed, they would then be signed by Mr. Prlic, and they would either be printed in the Narodni List or not depending on what decision they made. And I believe this -- now, with Article 18, which we discussed earlier, the assumption was that items which were outside of the usual purview of the HVO HZ HB would later be submitted to a meeting of the Presidency of the HZ HB, although in practice that wasn't really an issue because from October 17th, 1992, until the end of the HVO HZ HB the Presidency of the HVO HZ HB did not meet.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Just to clarify and perhaps I should have done it at the outset of this particular set of questions, the meeting notes that we've been looking at for the last few minutes, P 00391, these are minutes of a meeting of what you've just described as the Presidency and not of the -- what we've also called this afternoon the cabinet; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. And the Presidency that we're talking about -- that is conducting its business -- excuse me, in P 00391 is essentially what was the legislative branch of the Herceg-Bosna government at that time; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH
utterances.text: Yes. This was the Assembly with a representative from each municipality as opposed to the HVO HZ HB, which was the president and vice-presidents and six department heads.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: The executive branch.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH
utterances.text: Yes. Colloquially frequently called the cabinet.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, moving forward, in your report and in your inquiries did you find any particular symbols were adopted on behalf of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna or HVO, which is discussed at pages 73 and 75 of your report?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH
utterances.text: Well, yes. The HVO [sic] HZ HB had its own coats of arms and its own flag.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And were those adopted by decree or statute, or how were those symbols in fact adopted?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH
utterances.text: Those two items, the flag and the coat of arms, were adopted by the decree on the flag of the coat of arms of the HZ HB, which was signed by Jadranko Prlic on the 18th of November, 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I'm sorry. As this is all admittedly a bit confusing, on page 51, page -- line 4, I read "The HVO HZ HB had its own coat of arms." And if we go further down on line 9, we have a decree on the flag of the coat of arms of the HZ HB. Now, is it a coat of arms of HVO HZ HB or of HZ HB, which seems to me more probable. So line 4 falls to be corrected; is that correct? The "HVO" must be struck out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: In line 4.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, you're absolutely right. I misspoke.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Could I ask that the witness be shown on this point Exhibit P 00772.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And can you point out, sir, if you can on that page this part of the Narodni List if we have the decrees where the flag and coat of arms were, in fact, adopted?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH
utterances.text: Well, this entire decree is a decree on the coat of arms and flag of the Croatian community, and a lot of it is just instruction on how to display the flag, but the flag itself -- let's see here. It's very difficult for me -- here we go. Article 10. The flag of the HZ HB, it says it's described here as the red, white, and blue flag, and the coat of arms is the red and white chequerboard, both of which the coat of arms has been used as the symbol of the Kingdom of Croatia for centuries, and the red, white, and blue flag, with or without the coat of arms, has been used for the kingdom and then later incarnations of Croatia since 1848.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Keeping this document available to us, can you tell us, did the structures of the HVO or Herceg-Bosna adopt a form of currency?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH
utterances.text: Yes, they did. They adopted the Croatian dinar of the Republic of Croatia. All fines were to be paid and all fees were to be paid in Croatian dinars.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And in fact if we look at Article 15 of this same decree, on the next page, can you tell the Judges in terms of the penalties provided by this decree or statute, the penalties or fines would be paid in what currency?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH
utterances.text: They'd be paid in Croatian dinars. One thing to remember with this as well is that in 1992, 1993, there was extremely serious inflation with the Croatian dinars. So you see over and over in Narodni List they're changing the amount of the various fines and dinar amounts of fees and fines and so on to try and keep pace with the inflation of the Croatian dinars.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: So just for the matter of the record, when in the Narodni List or other documents we see reference in all caps to "HRD," that is the Croatian dinar?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH
utterances.text: Yes, it is, and that's the currency of the Republic of Croatia. During this period.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, as part of your research, sir, continuing on this topic in general, did you find that the laws and Statutes of Herceg-Bosna, the HVO, provided for what curriculum and what textbooks would be used in the schools of so-called Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH
utterances.text: Yes. And speaking very broadly, the textbooks and curriculum in use in all of the schools as well as the university in Mostar were those taken from the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And if I could ask that the witness -- we go back to an exhibit that we've looked at already, to the first semi-annual report which is P 00128. And directing your attention -- or please if I could have the usher's assistance to be to page 35 of that document which if I can read it should be ERN 00618512. Sir, could you just assist the Judges by pointing out various references on that page? This is from, again, the semi-annual report for the last six months -- or from the foundation to the end of 1992 of the HVO HZ HB referring to textbooks and curriculum of the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH
utterances.text: Yes. I believe this is from the section from the subdepartment on education and culture. They note that the primary schools at the beginning of the first paragraph there are taught according to the curricula of the community which are the curricula of the Republic of Croatia adjusted to their needs. And then in the next paragraph they say that all of the textbooks which they're using come from the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Very well. And turning to another topic, did you have opportunity to look in your work at the terminology used in connection with military ranks used in the Herceg-Bosna armed forces?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH
utterances.text: Yes, and they did change. They did -- there was legislation regarding the names for various ranks very early on.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And can you tell us what terminology was used by the HVO for the ranks of its armed forces? Where did this terminology come from?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH
utterances.text: They used the worth that were in use by the Croatian army of the republic of Croatia and were thought to be more Croatian than the other terms. For example, a captain is a "satinik" and not a "kapetan," and a major is not a major, he's a "bojnik," and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: In latter terms you've been using being the Croat terms?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH
utterances.text: Yes, yes. The ones that were in use by the HVO were the Croat terms, the ones which were thought of as being more Croat than the standard terms that had been used in the Yugoslav People's Army which were thought of as being Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you tell the Judges during this time, then, by the second half of 1992, what features or indicia of statehood did you see in connection with the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna?

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I object to that question. That's a matter which could only be answered by an expert in the field of international law. This witness has no qualifications to respond to what the indicia of statehood may be. Yes, it's also leading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What is your question, because you were interrupted.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, for example, Mr. President, I can ask a series of questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you tell the Judges, for example, was the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna -- did it enact laws?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You can answer that question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Oh, yes. It enacted legislation. It wasn't called laws using the Croatian term "zakon," but they enacted binding decrees and decisions.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Do you know whether a tax system was put in place?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH
utterances.text: Yes, it was. There were a number of taxes which were levied, including the war tax, which I cite in the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Was there a customs administration on the borders?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH
utterances.text: Yes, there was. And the customs were -- the level of -- or the rate at which customs were charged and waivers from customs duties were set by the HVO HZ HB.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Did it have a police force?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH
utterances.text: Yes, it did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Did it have an armed force -- the armed forces?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH
utterances.text: Yes, it did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: In reference to the laws or legislation as you mentioned a moment ago --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: May I add a question or two?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Did they issue passports or other documents to identify individuals?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, they didn't, but this is interesting. They did not issue their own passports. They issued identification cards. And they also, through their own Ministry of the Interior, encouraged people to apply for citizenship papers and passports of the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you. What about borders? Was the territory defined? Did they claim specific defined territory?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely. In the decision on the founding from what date is it exactly, the 16th of November, 1991 -- sorry, 18th of November, thank you, they list the municipalities, 28 municipalities, I think it is, which are supposed to be part of HZ HB, with the addition of small parts of two other municipalities. So 28 full municipalities and two sections of other municipalities. And it's very clearly defined.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One matter, sir, that was mentioned earlier on, a question that Mr. Scott could put to you, but I'll put it to you myself. Was there a currency?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, there wasn't a Herceg-Bosna currency as such. They used the currency of the Republic of Croatia as their currency, and it was officially declared to be the currency in use.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I saw that there was a decree that established a central bank. So there were no banknotes with the symbol of Herceg-Bosna on them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. They used banknotes with the symbols of the Republic of Croatia, which were similar but not identical to the symbols of Herceg-Bosna.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Where did these banknotes come from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Presumably from -- well, definitely from the Republic of Croatia. Presumably from the central bank of the Republic of Croatia in Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Earlier on you talked about inflation. These were dinars coming from Zagreb. If there was very high inflation in Herceg-Bosna, I don't know if you can answer my question, but did this have an impact in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, just to make this clear, it's the Croatian currency that has the problems with inflation up until about September of 1993, when it stabilised, and that has effects for Herceg-Bosna which is using the same currency, but it also had effects within the Republic of Croatia, because the Croatian dinar's their currency as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: An additional question regarding currency. That the period where in the former Yugoslavia the Deutschmark was used, and where was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I remember this very well because I was in the former Yugoslavia a lot of that period. Even before the dissolution of the former Yugoslavia beginning from, oh, at least the mid 1980s, there was very, very serious inflation within Yugoslavia, which only got worse as time went on, and for more and more things people were demanding hard currency, in particular Deutschmarks although other hard currencies were in use for a number of other things as well. With the dissolution of the former Yugoslavia the new Yugoslavia continued with its -- thank you. What was left of Yugoslavia still used the dinar. Republic of Slovenia introduced its own currency, the tolar, and the Republic of Croatia introduced us own dinars which then in 1994 were replaced by the kuna which still exists today. But for de facto purposes, it would have been very hard for any major purchase in Croatia, and I would suspect in Herceg-Bosna as well, to use Croatian dinars for any major purpose, because everyone knew at least from the middle of 1992 onwards the value was unstable, and so people would have preferred to use Deutschmarks and any other hard currency, although this was nothing which was done, as far as I know, officially any place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In your recollection, what was the annual inflation rate? Monthly rate.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, as a matter of fact, it kept increasing. It wasn't so bad in 1992, but it increased greatly in late 1993. I remember when we discussed -- or when this issue was discussed in another trial I put together just a sheet of the Deutschmark to dinar exchange rates in different months, and I don't remember the actual rate of inflation, but especially by the summer of 1993 it was -- it was quite severe. Probably not as bad as it was in what was left of Yugoslavia, in Serbia. That was even worse in this period. But if -- if it would be of assistance to you, I could bring that in during our next session. I think that particular document was entered as evidence in the Tuta-Stela case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That won't be necessary. I just wanted to have an idea of the situation. Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I could --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, since we're talking about background and context, and this is an important issue, perhaps the gentleman could tell us what currency was used in Bosnia-Herzegovina. How well was their central bank functioning? You know, what kind of currency was there, the inflation rate, and all the other things, since he wants -- tell us about the context in which this currency was being used along with the Deutschmark and everything else. That would be relevant, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Some additional information, Mr. Karnavas wants to have a comparison with Bosnia and Herzegovina. So as far as you can remember, what was the currency used in Sarajevo at the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, whatever currency was available, and currency wasn't very available in Sarajevo at that period. There was, and I didn't realise this until recently, there was such a thing as a Bosnia Herzegovinian wartime dinar but it wasn't used extensively at all. Generally speaking, foreign hard currencies were used. The Croatian dinar was used in the areas controlled by Herceg-Bosna, and the Yugoslav dinar was used to some degree in the Republika Srpska as well. Actually to large degree, although I mention the inflation problems there were even worse.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And what of the central bank, Your Honour? Was the central bank of Bosnia-Herzegovina functioning? And I would also -- since he mentioned it, until recently. How recently? The gentleman has been on the job for seven and a half years, fully, being paid, how recently was this revelation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Was the central bank in Bosnia-Herzegovina functioning, and at what time, if you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, unfortunately I can't tell you anything about the central bank of Bosnia based on documentation. All I can say based on what I did research for, for this paper is that I came across references to Bosnia and Herzegovina dinars being sent to local HVO governments in Central Bosnia. But as far as what the -- I didn't prepare to discuss the situation in Sarajevo, so I can't answer those questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One last question, a question already put to you by Mr. Karnavas. I'll ask it again because I find it interesting. In the area held by Herceg-Bosna and in the area held by the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, were inflation rates the same in these two areas as compared to the Deutschmark? Was there an inflation rate that was higher in one area than the other? Do you have any idea about this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, it's not so much a question of the areas as it is of the particular currencies. The Deutschmark remained fairly stable during this period. The Croatian dinar underwent a period of hyperinflation, and from what little I know about it, anecdotally I know there was very, very serious hyperinflation in what was left of the former Yugoslavia and Montenegro and Serbia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. You're not an expert in the field of the international monetary fund, so we'll not continue asking you these types of questions, but we might have the opportunity to come back to this during cross-examination. Mr. Scott, you can proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Before we began talking about all those matters, sir, I just put a question to you, some pages ago now, that you made reference to the adoption of legislation. And before moving on to another topic, can I ask that the witness be shown Exhibit P 00449. And while we're looking for that. Again I've been reminded to tender P 00772, which was the decree on the coat of arms and flag. Sir, I see -- you should have before you on the screen what has been marked as Exhibit 00449. Can you tell us what that is and again how that relates to your report?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH
utterances.text: This is the decree on the application of the Criminal Code of Bosnia and Herzegovina and of the former Socialist Federative Republic of Yugoslavia during state of war, imminent threat of war in Herceg-Bosna, and the law is adopted for use in Herceg-Bosna as long as it's not in contravention of any Herceg-Bosna legislation. I believe -- if I could scroll down a little bit farther. It doesn't say -- well, yeah. It also says in Article 2 that the dinar values in the old Bosnia and Herzegovina are already existing in Bosnia and Herzegovina Criminal Code will be converted into Croatian dinars and at this time it was still done at the same nominal value. I should correct myself, too. If we could scroll up a little bit farther. Yeah. I was confused as to the adoption of various Bosnian laws. In this particular instance, they don't mention that it's in effect -- they don't mention Herceg-Bosna law and its being possibly in contravention of the existing law and Herceg-Bosna taking precedence in this particular decree. That's another degree.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: We will tender, Your Honour, Exhibit P 00449.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I think later today -- changing topics a bit, later today we'll get to some charts, Mr. Tomljanovich, but I'm trying to be responsive to Judge Trechsel's comments and questions. I agree this can be sometimes confusing. Given the terminology you've used this afternoon, can you describe, summarise for us now what was the legislative -- what some would call the parliamentary or legislative body of Herceg-Bosna called during this time up to mid-1992, the second half of 1992?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH
utterances.text: The parliamentary or legislative function at that point was filled by the Presidency of the HZ HB.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And I think you touched on this already, but would you just briefly describe how that body was comprised? Who made the up the members of the Presidency and the terms in the sense of the legislative or Assembly?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH
utterances.text: That is mentioned in the founding declaration and it's either the highest Croat official of that municipality that's being represented or the highest representative -- or other highest representative of Croats, either the municipal leader or the highest Croat in the municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: When you say "highest Croat," what does that mean?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH
utterances.text: Well, generally speaking, I think the way it worked, although I'd have to look at the wording again to be absolutely sure --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: That's fine. Let's see if we can find it, then, please, so we don't guess.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH
utterances.text: And if I could make one request just to speed things up a bit?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH
utterances.text: If I could have hard-copy copies of these things. I had a binder available. It's much easier than having to look at --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: No objections, Your Honour. At least from this Defence, no objections.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If it's agreeable to all the Defence, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, to -- we can provide him with the folder to help him remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... who it's composed of, the presidency, he needs to look at a document. I mean, that's something that needs to be taken into consideration when viewing this person as an expert in this area.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: With the usher's assistance, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And if I could, I think -- I also have for my own purposes I created a binder of the original B/C/S documents. Now, the reason I wanted to refer to the precise wording in Exhibit 81, is because Article 7, which states who the Presidency should be composed of --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Excuse me. Could we also have displayed please, Exhibit P 00081.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH
utterances.text: The wording -- the -- the wording in Article 7 here is actually rather confusing. I think both in the B/C/S and in the English. I'll read the English translation. And that says that: "The leadership of the community shall be the Presidency, which shall consist of representatives of the Croatian people in the municipal government and the senior members or presidents of municipal boards of the Croatian Democratic Union or HDZ," which is -- that's a political party. Article 7, Exhibit 81. Now, I take that to mean, and as I said, the wording is a bit confusing in both the Croatian and in the English, that there is one --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would you lead the text in B/C/S, Article 7, so that the interpreters can interpret and we can compare it. So read it in the B/C/S and the English interpreters will give us the interpretation of it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Very well. [Interpretation] "Article 7. The supreme authority of the community shall be the Presidency comprising the representatives of the Croatian people in the municipal authority and those in the top-most functions, the most senior representatives, or the presidents of the municipal boards of the Croatian Democratic Union." [In English] It continues on, but that's not relevant to the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, when it makes reference of the -- to the municipal authority, what municipal authorities existed as of August 19 -- or excuse me, my apology, as of November 1991 when this decision was adopted? It makes reference to it the highest, the most senior representative -- I'm referring now to the English translation, the most senior representative of the Croatian people in the municipal authority. What municipal authorities is being referenced here?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH
utterances.text: Every municipality in Bosnia-Herzegovina, the 28 plus 2 that we're you can talking about in Herzegovina included all had their own municipal assemblies and their own municipal presidents. It's my understanding from reading this particular article that the representative should be and also from comparing this with the attendance lists at the meetings, that the representative to the Presidency should either be the president of the municipality or in the absence of the president of the municipality of being available the president of the municipal -- Municipal Board of the political party, the HDZ.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: It seems to me I have read in the report somewhere that one member of this Assembly, if I may call it like this, was a Muslim; is that correct? I was amazed when I saw it and I didn't understand. Maybe it's an error of mine.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't remember the Presidency of the HZ HB having a Muslim in it. I do recall that the cabinet of the HR HB had a Muslim in it and that there were Muslims present at the meeting of the HDZ in late 1992. It's possible that there was one, but I don't believe there was. At least not at the founding meeting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I was only asking. I'm not going to argue.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, I started this series of questions off by asking you to describe the -- what was the then legislative -- what some of us would call the legislative or parliamentary body. At this time what was the body which some might use the terminology to call the executive branch or the executive government. What was that body called?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH
utterances.text: That was officially known as the HVO HZ HB which was the cabinet of -- colloquially called the cabinet which had its own president, which was Mr. Prlic for most of this period, three vice-presidents, and six department heads.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, going back to that further explanation which I hope is helpful, can you tell the Judges then this body called the Presidency, which I -- for me I will say the legislature, from when did that body continue to meet? Can you tell the Judges what the situation was concerning the meeting or activity of that body between October of 1992 and August of 1993?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH
utterances.text: From October 17th, 1992, to August of 1993, the Presidency of the HZ HB, or legislative authority as you called it, did not meet, at least -- at least I can find no evidence of that in any available documentation.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Leaving the legislative power vested where?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH
utterances.text: We saw with the HVO HZ HB to act in its stead from October 17th, 1992, onwards, and we saw the decree on amending the -- decree on executive authority which allowed them to do that in situations where it was important to so.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Before moving on this point can we then look back to Exhibit P 00128. Once again, it's the first of the semi-annual reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: While that's coming up, Your Honours, can I, if it would be helpful, in answer to Judge Trechsel's question on page 75 of the report there is some information on the question that Your Honour raised about the presence of Muslims within the HVO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Thank you, Mr. Murphy.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, if you have that. I just -- we've looked at this one before, but if we can go down again to the bottom of that page, the language we looked at before and continuing on over to the second page. "However, in time the above rights and obligation were is expanded to a full legislative function." Is that report and document in fact consistent with your research and inquiries as you indicated just a moment ago, that in fact during this time the Presidency was not even meeting?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH
utterances.text: Yes, it's absolutely consistent. And no, as far as I can tell the Presidency was not meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Taking us back to the last phrase of that same paragraph that we looked at, meaning responsibility for determining policies for all spheres was in effect transferred to a certain extent to the HVO HZ HB. And is that what you found?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH
utterances.text: Yes, that was in fact the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now in looking at the composition of the Presidency that came back, whose reference in that decree that we were looking at a moment ago to the political party, the Croatian party the Croatian Democratic Union --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a moment, please. We understand that from October, 1992, to August, 1993, the Presidency did not meet and the legislation was in the hands of the HVO, the cabinet, in other words. Now, what is the reason -- you're the expert here, so why didn't the Presidency meet? Is there an explanation for that? Was it because of the state of war or was it because for some other reason? What would your explanation be as an expert of the fact that the Presidency from October -- after October didn't meet any more?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can only speculate based on the evidence that I've seen and that's in this report. My assumption, and this is just an inference I'm drawing from what I've seen in the other documentation, was that it would have been very difficult for the Presidency to all come together since its representatives from a number of different municipalities, it would not have been as quick as transferring these duties to the HVO HZ HB, which was meeting on and at least weekly basis during the entire period, but there's nothing in any of the documents I've seen that explicitly says why it's being done. Although in the decree amending the decision on executive authority they do mention that. They're doing this in cases not suffering delay. So I think it's in order to streamline wartime government and make decisions more quickly. Another problem as well is the president of the Presidency Mr. Boban - sorry; thank you - himself was frequently not in Bosnia-Herzegovina during this period but at negotiations outside the country. Different municipal chiefs would have been scattered all over Herceg-Bosna as well, so I can imagine and once again this is just speculation on my part that it would have been difficult to convene the Presidency frequently.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So am I to understand that there can be various hypotheses but there is no certainty in the matter. You can't know for sure why the Presidency didn't meet. These are your assumptions, right? The first being that Mr. Boban with respect to his diplomatic agenda was otherwise engaged, and on the other hand, the representatives of the different municipalities might have had difficulty in meeting. So those are your would assumptions but you can't tell us any more than that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, you're precisely correct and those are inferences I've made based on what I know from other documentation. There's no one document that says this is why this decision was made specifically. The only other thing I could add to that is that in meetings of the HVO HZ HB, I think on at least two occasions, members complain about the fact that they had -- that the Presidency of the HVO HZ HB has not met recently and that they're not pleased with the fact that the HVO HZ HB has become both an executive organ and a policy-making body. And that's mentioned once or twice in the minutes of the HVO HZ HB in their own meetings -- or of their own meetings. But, no, I can't -- I've never seen anything which specifically addresses why that decision was made on October 17, 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, on a constitutional level, the structure that you described to us, the Presidency seems to be the body that is above the HVO, and if this supreme body does not meet, this could perhaps explain the fact that certain members were surprised. Is that how you view the problem?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm not sure if there's a problem with the translation. Now, the Presidency of the HVO is responsible to the Presidency of the HZ HB in the sense -- pardon?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What I was saying is that the Presidency was made up of the representatives of municipalities or the most important Croats. So in fact it was a body, it was the principal body, the main body, and if that principal body did not meet for a number of months, for instance, it would be substituted, or it seems to have been substituted by the HVO.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, and I can be more specific about that. The Presidency was intended to be -- the Presidency of the HZ HB was intended to be the legislative Assembly. It's -- the duties and the sorts of legislation it was supposed to be tending to in this period from October 17th, 1992, onwards was dealt with by the HVO HZ HB, and it was the Presidency itself which passed this legislation allowing the HVO HZ HB to do exactly that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: On this point of the Presidency and that we were looking at the decree earlier, the decision earlier on the make-up of the Presidency, and it mentioned the Croatian Democratic Union or political party, can you please assist the Judges with was the -- did the party operate during this time period, that is, from mid-1992, approximately, to whenever you might be able to tell us in 19 -- at any point in 1993 where the party was exercising any substantial power over what was happening in Herceg-Bosna?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH
utterances.text: I should be a little more specific in my answer than the question is. We're talking about the HDZ BiH, which is the Bosnian branch of the HDZ, which is also the ruling political party in the Republic of Croatia at the time. During the period we're talking -- you're talking about in your question, from mid-1992 onwards, the party HDZ BiH does not seem to have exercised an awful lot of influence, at least certainly not based on the documentation which we have available. You had the -- you see from some of the exhibits that are mentioned in the report that the president of the party had misgivings about the HVO and the establishment of executive authority in the HVO. The upshot of all of that was Mr. Brkic was removed as president of the HDZ BiH and replaced by Mate Boban. The party -- there was a party meeting --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Excuse me, just a moment, because again some of this terminology, president this, Presidency that. When you said just now a moment ago Mr. Brkic --

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: -- this was the party president that followed Mr. Kljuic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely. He was in office from the winter to the fall of 1992 as leader of the HDZ BiH.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And were you indicating a moment ago, looking at the transcript, that Mr. Brkic had raised issues about the operations of the HVO HZ HB?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH
utterances.text: Yes, he had. And if you look at the exhibit which I included, which was minutes much a meeting or report on a meeting -- amongst other things report on a meeting in President Tudjman's office on I believe 5th of July, 1992, Mr. Brkic said that it wasn't clear what the HVO was supposed to be doing and made it fairly clear that none of this was being done in consultation with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And what happened to Mr. Brkic -- president Brkic after that, party president Brkic, excuse me.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH
utterances.text: I believe it was in October 1992, that he was removed as the HDZ BiH president as replaced by Mate Boban as HDZ BiH president. So when we look at the party meeting later that autumn in 1992, it's Boban who is presiding, not Brkic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, in that regard, then, if we could go to Exhibit P 00743.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: May I in between ask, removed by whom?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I have to make a distinction here between who he was removed by de jure and who he was removed by de facto. De jure I'm not entirely sure because we don't have an awful lot of party documentation from that period, and I haven't seen any official documentation from the HDZ BiH shedding like on that. However, de facto, if you look at the meetings of the 5th of July, 1992, and the 17th of September, 1992, at which Mr. Brkic was present with Mr. -- with President Tudjman, and if you keep in mind what happened to Mr. Kljuic, I think it's very clear that the ultimate decision on who would be the president of the HDZ BiH ultimately rested with the president of the HDZ of the Republic of Croatia and the global HDZ, and that was with Franjo Tudjman.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Perhaps, Judge Trechsel, he could clarify this party meeting later that autumn. Was it some kind of a meeting behind closed doors or was it a party congress?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If I can address that, it was in fact my next question in the document that we were just going to P 00743.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: In response to the question raised by the -- the issue raised by Mr. Karnavas just now, I think we will see that this is a record of a meeting -- I'll ask the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: As soon as you have it, Mr. Tomljanovich, can you tell us what this is?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH
utterances.text: Here we are. These are excerpts from the minutes of the HDZ BiH second general convention which, if not a completely public meeting, was certainly a broad meeting with a large number of people attending. It's a party congress, not a small meeting of the party central committee.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And can you take us to any particular language in this document, you made reference to it just a few minutes ago in your testimony, in reference to the activities or influence of the party in terms of Herceg-Bosna and the HVO during this time period?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH
utterances.text: In general, the declarations found in this document are supportive of the HVO HZ HB but don't go into any great detail on its functioning, nor is there really any debate on the HVO HZ HB.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: May I just ask for a clarification with regard to dates. I had noted that Mr. Tomljanovich had spoken about meetings on the 24th of July and 17th of September. This document relates to a meeting of 14 December. Could you perhaps clarify or is the date at the end of it only the date of when the record was written?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I can clarify that. There's three different meetings I was talking about. The first meeting chronologically is I believe the 5th of July, which is the meeting between HDZ BiH leaders as well as President Tudjman and some of his own domestic advisors in President Tudjman's office, and that meeting Brkic and the others discuss -- and Mate Boban is there as well. They discuss the question of Herceg-Bosna and what does this all mean in terms of the relationship between this new executive organ and the party. There's another meeting which is the presidential transcript of 17th of September, 1992, and that's many of the same individuals. That's Mr. Brkic, Mr. Prlic, and a number of other Croat leaders from Bosnia and Herzegovina with President Tudjman and a number other -- number of other persons from the Republic of Croatia present in the office. Now, this meeting here, Exhibit 00743, is the second general convention of the HDZ, and the date on that is the 14th of December, 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: With due respect, that is the date we have on the first page. On the last page we have a date of 14 November, 1992.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Just -- you're absolutely right. I had thought it was November, myself. Let me check the original here, 743. If I can look at the B/C/S version of this. Can I? Here we are. Yes, uh-huh. I'm looking now at the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: It's the same.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. No, it didn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Dates are the same.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Oh, yes, but it's not the same date as in the translation. Yes. At the beginning of the document it says 14th of November, 1992, in the original. This would appear to be a problem in the translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If I might just follow-up what the president did earlier. Could you just read the Croatian-language original on that particular portion and then we'll have the translators give us the -- interpreters give us the translation of that.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH
utterances.text: Yes, you mean at the top, the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "Mostar, the 14th of November, 1992."

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And that same mistake seems to have been made in reference then to item under "time and place where convention was held." If you can see that.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH
utterances.text: Yes. Just a second again. I've lost my place. But -- yes. I think it's also wrong in the translation there. Just a second. I've lost my place. Here we are, yes. Yes, it's also Studeni. It's also November.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: So the English translation stand corrected, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And it should be November, 1992. Before we leave this document, then, can you look at the -- toward the end of this document and tell us whether in fact it was at this meeting where you said a few moments ago that after Mr. Brkic, Mate Boban was appointed or elected president of the party HDZ BiH. Can you just point out to the Chamber where that is?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH
utterances.text: Yes. That's at Article 22. There's the election -- actually, this does tell you the de jure, the de jure basis for the election of Boban, although not the removal of Brkic. But it's under number 22. There's the election of Mate Boban as the president of the party.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President, I'm just going through my outline because some of these documents we've covered, and I won't cover them again if we don't have to.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And for the point -- for clarification purposes, I would object to this being considered a meeting. It's a party convention. There's a big difference between a regular meeting and a party convention where you can see we have all these delegates who are deciding who is to be elected. I think Tony Blair is facing similar pressures. So this is something that really needs to be distinguished.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. It's -- looks more like a convention or a Congress than a meeting. Therefore, the term "convention" gives us a better idea. It reflects better what sort of meeting it was about, a meeting between a number of people.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, we certainly accept the language of the document itself which appears in the English translation, at least to use "convention." In my notes, in fact, it was referred to as the party general assembly. I think everyone was using "meeting" in a broad sense of a gathering of people. I'm happy to use the word "convention." Mr. President, I think we may be approaching the second break, if this is an appropriate time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. It's time for the break. We'll resume at five to 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Scott, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: My apology. I'm trying to comply with the Court's direction today. Maybe it's better if we catch up today because if we go to 7.00 I know everyone will be anxious to leave the courtroom. So far we have specifically addressed and we would tender -- the Prosecution would tender the following documents: P 00947, which is the complete Narodni List for 1992. P 05166, which is the Narodni List for 1993. P 07435 and P 07439 which together comprise the full Narodni List for 1994. Then in addition, Exhibits P 00305, P 00069, which I think was previously admitted but checking -- no, I'm told it's not. P 00069. P 00079, P 09526. I understand that P 007 -- excuse me, 152 was previously admitted. If it hasn't been previously admitted, we would tender it now. P 00303, P 00440, P 00684. And the last document that we used before the break was P 00743.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, if we can move forward, then, Mr. Tomljanovich. In the course of conducting your research and preparing your report, can you tell the Judges whether you found indications that the establishment of Herceg-Bosna and the institutions as you've described them this afternoon, whether that was accepted under the law of the -- of Bosnia-Herzegovina and by the Muslim side? If you -- or party.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH
utterances.text: Yes. The establishment of the HVO HZ HB and indeed the very establishment of the HZ HB was declared unconstitutional by the Constitutional Court of BiH, aside from all of the other misgivings which I mentioned in the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And for the record, and I believe it's been previously admitted, if the registry can confirm this, P 00476, is a copy of the Constitutional Court decision from 14 September, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Has that been admitted previously? No. I thought it had. My apology. If the witness can then be shown, please, P 00476.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I believe -- I had thought the Judges had seen this document before, but can you briefly tell us, Mr. Tomljanovich, what this document is and how it enters into your analysis?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH
utterances.text: Yes. This is the decision of the Constitutional Court of Bosnia and Herzegovina from 14th of September, 1992, signed by the president of the court, and their decision is to annul most of the founding legislation of the HZ HB and the HVO HZ HB, and it includes things like the --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Excuse me. If you could scroll down, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH
utterances.text: Yeah. It's -- all nine decisions which are nullified here are listed one by one beginning with the decision of the establishment the HZ HB and then going on to the amendments to it. And a good deal although not all of the legislation which was passed on the 3rd of July, 1992. But certainly the most basic ones such as the statutory decision on the temporary establishment of the executive authority. Nullifying these founding documents would have the net effect of nullifying the whole body of the HZ HB and of the HVO HZ HB as unconstitutional. Just very briefly, the argument here is that the Herceg-Bosna is not an association of municipalities as would have been allowed by the constitution of Bosnia and Herzegovina, that it went beyond the sorts of things which should be allowed or are allowed in the constitution.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. In terms of the structures and processes of the HVO and Herceg-Bosna that you've researched, do the records of those structures and processes indicate any awareness by the leadership of the Herceg-Bosna entity or the HVO that the creation of these bodies, the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna and the HVO HZ HB had been rejected under the law of Bosnia-Herzegovina and by the Muslim party?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH
utterances.text: I cite in the report the correspondence between the Constitutional Court and the Croat authorities regarding this matter prior to the decision. Certainly the problems in getting the Muslim side to accept the HVO is mentioned many times after that. I didn't cite -- I've only seen one instance of a document from someone in the HDZ BiH directly answering this, and I didn't include that in this report because he's not one of the persons either accused or -- in this trial. So that I did not put in, although I had seen that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you tell -- excuse me. Can you please be shown Exhibit P 00543. Can you tell us what this is, sir? And it may be -- I'm not sure again, but it may be the first of the actual minutes of the HVO HZ HB, which had been much discussed this afternoon but the first actual minutes that we've seen. Can you describe those to us generally, and if that's consistent with the kind of record you've seen being minutes of this body?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH
utterances.text: First of all, I believe there was a meeting that -- prior to this for which we have minutes, but this -- this set of minutes here follows the format. All of them do. The session is numbered, and this is the fifth session of the HVO HZ HB. It always states the date and time at which it was held and where exactly it was held, which isn't always the same over the course of the existence of the HVO HZ HB. They always begin mentioning that Mr. Prlic is the president and chairing the meeting, and then they list all attendees. And then they mention that -- they always then move on to the agenda of the meeting, which was proposed by the president. And then the minutes of the meeting following -- generally speaking follow the agenda in the meeting itself. Usually the last item on the agenda is something like, yes, either current issues or miscellaneous business. But in its format and length, this is a very typical meeting. They always follow the same format and form.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Could I direct your attention to item number 8 on page 5. Do the minutes indicate that Mr. President, well, here Mr. President of the HVO HZ HB, gave a report?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH
utterances.text: Yes, that's true. And in this particular instance the only president they would be referring to would be the president of the HVO HZ HB, which is Mr. Prlic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And if we continue over to page 6. Now, I don't want to read the entire page. Report about dealings and communications between the Croatian and Muslim people, it says, in the second line.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And can I direct your attention to the last sentence on that page, and can you read that, please?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH
utterances.text: Beginning with "The key political question."

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: No, the last sentence beginning on page 6 itself?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH
utterances.text: "However, the Muslim side ..."?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, please?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH
utterances.text: Reads "However, the Muslim side does not recognise the existence of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna considering it to be a break-up of Bosnia-Herzegovina."

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Does the document go on then to indicate apparently a report by Mr. Stojic at this same meeting, on page 7?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH
utterances.text: Yes, it does, concerning military reorganisation. He reports on the situation of the HVO commanders. And he also, in the very last item, recommends -- recommends setting up military courts and military prosecutors' offices saying that's necessary for efficiency and the strengthening of military discipline.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, we tender Exhibit P 00543. Your Honours, I would like now to turn to what's now been marked as P 09689, which is the booklet of organisational charts that has been provided to counsel and the Court last week. The booklet, if you want to call it that, the compilation as a whole has been given the Exhibit number P 09689. The people in the courtroom may have their hard copies or I'm told it's also available in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Referring to page 1 of that exhibit, sir, I don't know if you prefer to use it -- look at it on the screen or if you prefer to have a hard copy in front of you.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH
utterances.text: I would prefer to have a hard copy if I could. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Tomljanovich, if I can direct your attention primarily being to what might be called the upper half of the page. The title of this document or chart is "Political and military --" excuse me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Counsel Ibrisimovic has the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. The document wasn't on the 65 ter list that we received, and on the basis of your guidelines and your ruling, the Prosecutor did not tell -- did not ask for the document to be listed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, Mr. Ibrisimovic may be right on that respect. These were charts that were distributed before Christmas last year to all counsel and to the Court. In fact, prepared at the Court's request. And if they were not on that list, that's certainly an oversight, but counsel's been aware of these charts for at least 9 or 10 months.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Counsel Ibrisimovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. These charts were sent with the material on the 23rd of December, but they were not on the 65 ter list.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I agree, Your Honour. They were not on the list. They were disclosed in December. I apologise for the oversight, but again, counsel's had them for approximately 10 months now. May I continue, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If you look at the top right corner of the document, it is labelled "Political and military organisational structure of the HZ HB (until 20 November 1993)." Now, Mr. Tomljanovich, can you tell me -- first of all, can you tell the Judges did you play a role in the preparation of this chart, or at least parts of this chart?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I didn't actually physically put the chart together, but I was consulted for factual accuracy of what's basically the top and the left-hand of the chart.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, in terms of what we've discussed so far this afternoon, looking -- we see Boban, we see Prlic, the HVO HZ HB, we see the HZ HB Presidency out to the upper left part of the chart. Can you tell the Judges whether you find these portions of the chart to be consistent with your report and your findings or observations?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH
utterances.text: Yes, they are.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: The description and the role of the Presidency, the HZ HB Presidency, again the box in the upper-left portion of the overall chart and the way it is portrayed here, again does that -- is that accurate to the best of your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH
utterances.text: Yes, it is. The HZ HB Presidency in the upper left-hand corner, who was in it is described here with a slightly different translation than we saw on the other exhibit. It's also shown with the line that they elect the president of the HVO HZ HB, and the presidents responsible to them. Mr. Mate Boban presides over it. And from the bottom, from the municipalities, you see that it's people from the municipalities, the representatives, who are in the HZ HB Presidency.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: You made a brief reference early this afternoon that in addition to the departments -- well, let me go back. Sorry. Strike that. In the box that is marked "HVO HZ HB," and with Mr. Prlic being the president, are the departments that you've identified earlier this afternoon, are all those departments indicated in that box?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH
utterances.text: Yes, all six are there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, what I started to say was you also indicated briefly this afternoon that apart from departments there were also other things called commissions, services, and other administrative bodies, and do you see that portrayed on the chart?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH
utterances.text: Yes. That's over in the left-hand side here, and there's just selected ones of particular importance, I think, for the case that are selected here. There are certainly far more of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH
utterances.text: And they're directly subordinated to the HVO HZ HB all of these commissions, services, and other bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. We'll be coming back to some of the other charts in the course of your examination-in-chief. I'll be moving off that chart, Mr. President and Your Honours, unless you have questions that you want to put at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, about this organisation chart. On the right we see Petkovic, Praljak, and then Petkovic again. And if we go back up, we see that this square, there's a link with this square to Mate Boban, the Main Staff, and then we see that there's a link-up with Mr. Bruno Stojic. So when we look at this chart, do we have to understand the following: Does this mean that the military chain of command obeyed directly or was directly under the command of Mate Boban whilst being subordinated to Stojic? That's what I see on this chart.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I believe the answer to that is found in the order on -- I forget if it's an order or decree on the internal organisation of the Defence Department. That mentions that the Main Staff is within the Defence Department and that it is responsible both to Mate Boban, president -- well, it doesn't mention Boban by name. It mentions that the president of the HZ HB is the commander-in-chief, and that for other purposes they also answer to the head of the department for defence, who was Bruno Stojic. But the different ways in which they're responsible to both is spelled out there explicitly.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Again, we'll come back is to some other parts of the chart or other charts in the course of your testimony. If we could then turn specifically, in fact, to the Department of Defence. Could I ask you to go to Exhibit P 00586. And as soon as you have that, Mr. Tomljanovich, if you can tell us what that is and how it enters into the work that you did.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH
utterances.text: This document is the decision on the basic principles of the organisation of the Defence Department signed on 15th of September, 1992, by Mate Boban, and it's forwarded on the -- this copy has been forwarded. The cover letter is also attached here. But this decision, if we look at section B on page 5 in the English translation, I think answers Judge Antonetti's question directly. It says here in section B -- yeah, right there. "The man stay of the Croatian Defence Council shall be part of the department. "The Chief of the Main Staff shall head the Main Staff." And here it explicitly says: "The chief of the Main Staff shall be responsible to the head of the department proposing and implementing measures for all administrative tasks and issues relating to the budget and material supplies and to consumption and general organisation of civilian life, as well as wartime organisation of the Armed Forces." And then the next paragraph below that says: "The Chief of the Main Staff shall be directly responsible to the president of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna for all issues relating to the Supreme Command, unit organisation, strategic and operative plans, and the use of the armed forces in ... war or peace." I'm sorry, "... in times of war or peace."

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Is there anything in particular else about this document before moving. I certainly don't intend to go through every part of the document, but is there anything more about this document as it relates to your analysis that you'd like to point out?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH
utterances.text: Well, it's also useful in that it lays out the responsibilities of the deputy head and his leadership of the civilian section on page 3. It lists the four deputy heads of the Defence Department on page 3, and lists the offices and administrations under the assistants as well. And then finally, just sort of as a catch-all, but it's important to note, Article 15 at the very end of this document on the last page, page 7, notes that the "The inner organisation of the Main Staff, the command and control of the Main Staff's internal organisational units and other relations shall be determined by the Chief of the Main Staff with the approval of the head of the department and the president of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna."

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: So going back to your chart a moment ago, this would in fact be consistent with that -- there was -- there was a chain, if you will, a line going from the head of the Main Staff both to the president of the HZ HB and to the head of the Department of Defence; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH
utterances.text: Yes, and for reasons laid out in section B of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Very well. We will tender Your Honour, Exhibit P 00586.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I would like to put a follow-up question regarding page 5 and the last but one paragraph. There we read: "The Chief of the Main Staff shall exercise superior authority over the Command of the Croatian Defence Council, within the scope of general and specific powers vested in him by the President of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna." Now, Croatian Defence Council I think is HVO, but it's a different meaning of HVO. Could you perhaps elaborate?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I read it as saying that the Chief of the Main Staff is in fact the commander of the army under the president, but I'll listen.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, to make it clear at this point, it is confusing. The term HVO depending on the context is used in documents in many different ways. Sometimes the HVO can mean the HVO HZ HB and talk about the cabinet, the executive cabinet. Sometimes when people HVO, they're generically referring to all the Herceg-Bosna authorities or they're generically referring to what in official documents is usually called the armed forces of the HZ HB. Another use of the term HVO is with the municipal executive authority. The municipal executive authority in Livno, for example, would be called the Livno HVO. So if someone talks about the municipal HVO, that's the municipal executive authority. The HVO is also the governing cabinet. It's also used for the military armed forces and it's also sometimes generically, colloquially for all Herceg-Bosna institutions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Now, why does it say here that "the Chief of the Main Staff shall exercise authority over the command of the Croatian Defence council"? Not over the Croatian Defence Council. Could you explain that, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I will have to look. It might help if I take a look quickly at the original in B/C/S. Here we go. Maybe it would help, or maybe it wouldn't help if I read the original B/C/S into the record as well. I'll do it and we'll see what it says. [Interpretation] "Within the scope of the principal and concrete authorisation of the president of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, the Chief of the Main Staff is superior to the command of the Croatian Defence Council."

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can we then go on, please, to Exhibit --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If I may interject here. Just a point of clarification, because obviously this is very confusing. The gentleman indicated that he reads B/C/S. I assume that he's read these documents in the original as well as the translation. He indicated that he had analysed and synthesised or synthesised and analysed, I can't remember which came first, assuming, you know, I would suspect analyse and synthesise, perhaps he could give us the interpretation, what does this mean and, if he consulted with anybody to try to figure out in the event that he didn't understand it when he read it, because obviously there seems to be some confusion. So I think we need to figure out to what extent this gentleman has gone through to understand this, because he's rendering opinions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I would reformulate your question in asking what is the meaning, if any, of the word "command" here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My suspicion or my opinion based on comparing this with the Law On Defence and all the other multitude of military documents that I've seen over the past few years is that this is poorly written, but what Mr. Boban was trying to say is that the Chief of the Main Staff exercises military command over the various military commanders of the armed forces of the HZ HB.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If we can then go on to Exhibit P 00588.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: It may or may not shed any light on this, but could you tell us what that exhibit is, please?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH
utterances.text: This is the revised decree on the armed forces. That's not what we have right now on the screen. There we are. It's the decree on the armed forces of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, and this regulates the armed forces of Herceg-Bosna. I should point out that this is the revised decree from 17th October, 1992. The initial decree was issued on the 3rd July, 1992. I discussed some of the differences in my report which are relatively minor, with the exception that in the revised decree there is a great deal of information on mobilisation and the draft which were not present in the original decree on defence. It -- it's a very long document. It defines the military. Under Article 3, it lists the obligations of every citizen of the HZ HB to the military and begins by saying: "Each citizen of the HZ HB has an obligation to protect and defend the independence and territorial integrity of the HZ HB and, with relation to the above, especially in the following," and lists the five ways in which citizens are bound to assist the armed forces of HZ HB, then moves on to the work obligation of all adults, Civil Defence. Beginning with Article 9, it lists the competencies of the HVO and the bodies of the HZ HB in matters of defence. Continues on through Articles -- and it also outlines the various offices and administrations and their duties and those of other bodies. Defines the armed forces in Article 21. And I'll only point out here at this point in Article 24, the armed forces are defined as consisting of peacetime and wartime troops. And then it's here, Articles 29 through 32, that the leading and commanding of the armed forces, the sorts of issues we were just talking about are addressed. And then it moves on to discuss reinforcement of the armed forces, military duty, and mobilisation. And we won't go through all of those. It's a very long document, and I won't go through all of the particular sections there, but we'll just leave it with Articles 29 through 32, which once again define the role of the Supreme Commander.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please go back to Article 29, point 2, about the role of the Supreme Commander, the president. How do you interpret point 2 of this article?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I myself have not seen a plan of utilisation as such referred to.
