I suspect that, and other documentation would seem to indicate this, that the commander-in-chief is -- well, honestly, I can't say anything than what's in -- than what's in that particular line. Now, speculating on that, I assume --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I will object to any speculations unless the Trial Chamber is asking for speculation, in which event, you know, I won't object, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. Without speculating, apparently according to point 2 we get the certainty that the president makes decisions with regard to the utilisation of armed forces and with regard to their use on the ground. Based on the documents you've reviewed, have you found any orders issued by Mate Boban to the Ministry of Defence or to the head -- the Chief of Staff to conduct military operations in various areas? Have you seen anything of the kind?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I have not, but I should make it very clear that as the charge I'd been given with this report was to discuss the governing and political structures, I didn't undertake to get a comprehensive view of all of the military orders. I didn't review all of the orders of the Chief of the Main Staff, and I didn't review all of the incoming orders to the Chief of the Main Staff. And my answer would be no, I have not seen that, but I would also add that in this particular instance I wasn't looking for that either because that was not my understanding of what the scope of my report was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. Tomljanovich --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If we could then go on very quickly to touch on several additional documents just to see how they fit in this structure. Of course, we do tender, if we have not already, P 00586 and P 00588. If I could ask you to be shown Exhibit P 00293. And I'll just asking you as that's being pulled up and you're looking for it, can you tell -- confirm for the Judges that the Department of Defence of the HVO had Rules of Military Discipline?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH
utterances.text: Yes, it did, and I believe the exhibit number you just mentioned are the Rules of Military Discipline. Let's see here. Yes, Exhibit 293. The Rules of Military Discipline, which is another one of the orders or pieces of legislation, enactments that was passed on the 3rd July, 1992, by the Presidency of the HZ HB and signed by Mate Boban, and it's 111 -- 112 articles on military discipline.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can I ask you to go to Exhibit P 00951. And can you tell us what that is, please, if you have it?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH
utterances.text: Yes. This is the decree on the establishment of a military industry office signed by Jadranko Prlic, 9th of December, 1992, and it establishes this military industry office which is supposed to regulate military production. Just a number of things. It gives orders to the producers, approves contracts on import and experts --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Just a moment. When you talk about military production, can you give the Judges an idea of what's being talked about here? What is military production, or if you can refer to a particular section?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH
utterances.text: It's the -- it's supposed to regulate the production of weapons within the HZ HB. Its duties are enumerated in Article 2. There is a number of them there. It's also to monitor and oversee the military industry and monitor the situation. I won't read out all of the different things it's charged with.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH
utterances.text: The only thing I should mention, which seems a bit strange if you're not familiar with the topic, is Article 4 mentions that the headquarters of the office will be in Travnik, or the temporary headquarters will be in Travnik and not in Mostar which --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Why would that be the case, sir, if you can assist the Judges?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH
utterances.text: Well, the area of Central Bosnia is the area in which most of the arms factories were located. The idea in the old Yugoslav system would be that arms factories would be located in the centre of the country, the most remote and hard to get to part, so there's important arms factories in Travnik, Novi Travnik, and Vitez, right in that region, so it would make sense for the office to be there where the factories are.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you next please look at P 02707. 2707. I don't think that's what I see on e-court new. It should be -- if ERN will assist the registry, 00507630. There we are. Can you tell the Judges, sir, what this is and when it was issued and by who?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH
utterances.text: I don't have it in hard copy but -- yes, yes, I know this. This is the entire issue of Narodni List for June -- the 11th issue in June of 1993, and it's the "decision on carrying out mobilisation in the territory of the HZ HB in times of the immediate threat of war or wartime," and it's signed, if we could go to the bottom, signed by Jadranko Prlic on the 10th of June, and this orders full mobilisation and goes into details of how people are to report for mobilisation. I should also note that this was done very quickly. Generally speaking the practice in Narodni List is they would wait until they had a full issue of enactments and then publish an issue. This was publish as an issue unto itself. So the implication is that time was very pressing with this particular decision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: May I ask a question of -- of detail.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Article 5 requires men working abroad of which there were quite a number --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: --before expiry of their work permit to report to a relevant defence office. Were offices established abroad or was this an office which would be within Herceg-Bosna?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, my understand and before answering this question I should add there is separate legislation on the military duties of persons working abroad. There is separate decree or order for that. I assume when "defence office" is used here usually it's a term of art meaning the local municipal office. I don't remember off the top of my head if a separate office was set up abroad, but I assume from Article 5 that we're talking about the Defence office in the municipality in which this person comes from in Herceg-Bosna, although off the top of my head I don't remember everything it says in the decree regulating the military obligations of people living abroad. And there is a specific piece of legislation for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Looking at this document, the B/C/S version, in fact, I see that the number 11 in the text of the -- of year II, Mostar, the 10th of June, can you explain that? Why does it say year II, number 11, year II, Mostar? What's the year II? May we have your explanation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That would be the second year of existence of the Narodni List. This is the 11th -- the 11th issue of the Narodni List for the second year in which it existed, because 1992 being the first year, 1993 being the second. It's not a reference to anything in the French Revolution and restarting the number of years. It's not -- I don't think it's that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: There were -- it may assist before we leave this document in Article 2 it makes references to defence offices in all municipalities and in reference to one of your answers to the Judges, was it your understanding that there were various defence offices out in the various municipalities that were charged with such things as mobilisation, conscription?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH
utterances.text: Yes, there were, and that's all mentioned in the law on defence and the other founding legislation regarding defence. Municipal -- municipalities had defence offices, and above them were defence administrations which, I think, corresponded to the operational zones. So there would have been four of them. And their duties, I think, are spelled out in the law on defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Could I next -- and I'll tender some of these exhibits all at one time?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH
utterances.text: Oh, excuse me. On the decree on defence, not the law on defence. I misspoke.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. I was just saying I will tender some of these documents as a group when we finish. Can I next ask the witness to be shown P 07041. And as soon as it you have, Mr. Tomljanovich, if you could he will it us what that is and how it relates to the defence functions of Herceg-Bosna.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH
utterances.text: This is the decree on the manufacture and trade of arms and military equipment in times of the immediate threat of war or in wartime in the territory of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna. If we could move down to the bottom for the date and the signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Next page, please.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH
utterances.text: Yeah. It's signed by Jadranko Prlic on the 6th of December, 1993. And this regulates the movement and production of arms on their territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Could I ask you, Mr. Tomljanovich, to check -- once again to check the dates, because in the --

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: -- in the English translation of the introduction to the statute, if you will, or decree, it says this was adopted at its session 6th January, 1993, unless it's referring to some underlying statute.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH
utterances.text: Excuse me, what's the -- I don't have this in the translation in my binder. What is the exhibit number again, please?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH
utterances.text: I also don't have that in this particular binder. Could I look the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If the registry could show ERN 00507646.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH
utterances.text: Okay. If we could just scroll down a tiny bit. There we are. And now in the preamble, it says that this was adopted at the HVO HZ -- HVO HZ HB meeting of the 6th of January of 1993. And if we could scroll down to the bottom. Next page. Yes. The date there is 6th of December. Now, since the serial number is a 1993 -- well, this is strange. The serial number is a 1993 serial number but it is a very low serial number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: It is even stranger than this is in the Gazettes of 1993 and it anticipates a decision of 6 December of the same year so something must be wrong.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It would have to be -- could we go back to the preamble again? Yeah. See? It's from the 1993 Gazette, and of course the HZ HB -- HVO HZ HB didn't exist by January of 1994 -- by December of 1993. So this has to be January of 1993. The other reason I say that is because the serial number at the end is a very low 1993 serial number. If we could move to the serial number at the bottom next to Mr. Prlic's signature. Now, it's a 1993 serial number. From October of 1992 onwards, everything signed by the office of Mr. Prlic or by Mr. Prlic himself had a number and the Croatian word you see that to the left of his significant for number is "broj." All of his documents have the number 01, hyphen, I, hyphen, the serial number within that year, slash, the number of the year. So I know there were hundreds of documents in 1993, so this would have had to have been very early in the year and so it has to be January of 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: With all that in mind, then, could we -- could I ask you was there also a decree or decision of the HVO armed forces or defence department on the treatment of captured persons?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH
utterances.text: Yes, already from the summer of 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Could I ask you be shown please Exhibit P 00292. And as soon as you have that, Mr. Tomljanovich, can you tell us what that is?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH
utterances.text: Yes. This is the decree on the treatment of persons captured in armed fighting in the HZ HB, signed on the 3rd of July, 1992. I believe by Mate Boban, although I can't see here. In Article 1 it states that -- yeah, Mate Boban. It states that, "persons captured will be treated in accordance with international law and the Geneva Conventions of 1949." It specifically mentions the Yugoslav people's army but also mentioned any other persons captured in armed fighting against the HZ HB. In Article 2, and this is regarding the location of camps [sic] for prisoners, says that the head of the justice and administration department in cooperation with the head of the defence department and the head of the department of the internal affairs or interior shall designate the locations where prisoners shall be kept in accordance with Article 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, we tender P 00293, P 00951, P 02707, P 07041, and P 00292.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd just like to ask a clarification. Looking at Article 2 here, and, as far as I can read, it would appear that the locations where prisoners shall be kept should be -- shall be designated by at least three departments, the justice department, the defence department, and the Department of the Interior. So is that how you as an expert understand this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's how I understand it. We'll see in other exhibits that at least the Defence department and justice department did so together in one instance, and as far as we can tell from the documentation, this -- in another instance this procedure was not followed. But it's my understanding that it should be according to this second article, that they should be planning the locations, all three persons together, in cooperation with each other, head of the defence department, head of the justice department, head of the department for the interior.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The text that we're looking at, was it after the 30th of July, 1992? Was it modified after that date or abridged or anything, or in 1993 did it still have its juridical force, legal force?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I know and can remember, I've never seen any amendment or overturning of this particular decree. As far as I can tell, there was nothing that can overturn it or no longer put it in force.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mr. Scott, we've got five more minutes left, but I can see Mr. Murphy on his feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: Yes. Your Honour, I wonder if the witness might be given an opportunity to correct the record at page 99, line 25, when he talks about camps and there is no reference whatsoever in Article 2 to camps. It merely talks about locations. Clearly that's -- that would be a highly prejudicial error to remain in the record, and perhaps the witness would care to correct it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. Tomljanovich --

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH
utterances.text: Yes. Could I quickly look at the B/C/S copy of this again? If we could scroll down to number 2. Yes. Yes, you're absolutely right. It's "locations," not "camps," in this instance.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Would you also in at that regard, excuse me, look at Article number 3 and what terminology is used to describe --

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM TOMLJANOVICH
utterances.text: Yes. In Article number 3 it says that the department for defence will manage the locations mentioned in Article 2 of this order or of this decree. So that after the locations have been determined by all three departments, the Department of Defence would then be responsible for the management of these locations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Does that mean that those locations were under the control of the Ministry of Defence or Department of Defence? Because under Article 3, that is the ministry that manages that them.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, it's still the Department of Defence here. It's not the ministry. Yes, I understand that this they are managing or directing these locations, and that they're responsible for their activities. It's absolutely, I translate "upravlja" as "manages." I don't know what it is in the English. Can we see the English again? "In charge," okay. Or "directs," you could say as well. I think they're all correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You said something earlier on. The Department of Defence might come -- be under a different authority, not the Ministry of Defence, because in Article 2 we see there are three. There's the justice -- there's justice, the interior, and defence, and Article 3 seems to link this charge to the defence department. They're in charge. Do you know that or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, my reading of this is that in Article 2, the three different departments are in charge of designating where these locations. Once they're established, Article 3 charges the department of defence with managing them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, I see the time, and I think if we could conclude. There's one additional exhibit I need to tender. I've been told that in fact P 00476 had not been previously admitted. I thought that it had been, but we would tender and do tender P 00476.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I guess I have one last point of clarification based on the questions that were posed by the Trial Chamber. It seems to me the gentleman is reading a document and giving an interpretation of the document based on a reading that any normal human being, you know, layperson, you know, could reach. Is that the case or is he using any particular knowledge as an expert in this particular area and is imparting his opinion based on his expertise something that we're incapable, and that's why we have this gentleman here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Defence is going back once again to the same problem. So in a few seconds, when you answer a question asked of you, are you basing your opinions on the simple reading of the text in front of you, or are you giving an answer on the basis of your expert knowledge of studies of the many decrees, documents, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In this particular instance my answer was based not just on the fact that I can read this document in both languages but that I know all of the documents surrounding it, what in fact the practice was following the adoption of this document and everything -- it's informed by everything else I've seen, how I read that. So it's informed by everything else, not simply by my ability to read it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. It's time to close for the day. Mr. Scott, the registrar has told me that you've used two hours and 12 minutes so far. As it's 7.00 p.m., we reconvene tomorrow morning at 2.15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 5th day of September, 2006, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.02 p.m.,
